Diagnose probable oesophageal candida (mouth symptoms page)
rules.problem: AND with white patches is justified: the swallowing box hangs under the white-patches column.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable herpes simplex (mouth symptoms page)
rules.problem: Trigger is any blister on lips or in the mouth; page says 'Painful blisters'. Diagnosis concept is the general 'Herpes simplex' where 'Oral herpes simplex infection' exists. Type and probable level are right.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable aphthous ulcer (mouth symptoms page)
rules.problem: Trigger 'Ulcer of mouth' is broader than the page's 'Painful ulcer/s with central white patch': every recorded mouth ulcer becomes aphthous ulcer probable. Type and probable level are right.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable angular cheilitis (mouth symptoms page)
Diagnose probable impetigo around the mouth (mouth symptoms page)
rules.problem: Requiring the angle-of-mouth fissure is justified: the impetigo line sits inside the 'Red, cracked corners of mouth' column.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable contact dermatitis at corners of mouth (mouth symptoms page)
Diagnose possible diabetes from dry mouth (mouth symptoms page)
rules.problem: 'check for diabetes' -> possible is right; OR over thirst/frequency/weight loss is a fair reading of the comma list.

rules.rule: Diagnose possible anaphylaxis from mouth symptoms
rules.problem: Structure (swelling AND any of the list) and 'check for' -> possible match the red box. Only the generic Food exposure is loose (c067).

rules.rule: Urgent: mouth symptoms with inability to open mouth or anaphylaxis signs
rules.problem: Urgent is justified by the red-box heading and 'Refer urgently'; (unable to open mouth) OR (swelling AND any-of) is the page's structure. Generic Food exposure (c084) can make the Urgent branch fire on swelling + having eaten.

summary: Nothing is invented: every condition traces to the page and all 45 SNOMED concepts resolve. The most consequential looseness is the aphthous ulcer rule, whose trigger 'Ulcer of mouth' drops 'painful' and 'central white patch', so any mouth ulcer is diagnosed as aphthous ulcer probable; the herpes simplex rule similarly drops 'painful' and uses the general Herpes simplex concept where Oral herpes simplex infection exists. The allergen branch uses a generic 'Food' exposure with the footnote's 'within the past few hours' window dropped, which feeds both the possible anaphylaxis rule and the Urgent priority. Not invented but missing from the rules: 'anaemia likely' (Hb < 12 g/dL woman / < 13 g/dL man) in the angular cheilitis column, and the header's abacavir -> AHR check.
